prompts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: visual target concept for a 2D pixel-art Hong Kong walking RPG, NOT an actual screenshot. Landscape 16:9 composition. A single coherent street scene inspired by Canton Road, Tsim Sha Tsui: upscale glass retail frontage on one side, narrower Hong Kong commercial facades with air conditioners on the other, grey pavement, curb railings, pedestrian crossing and a red Hong Kong taxi. A recognisable Apple store frontage is the commercial anchor; smaller 7-Eleven striped signage and McDonald's golden arches appear as supporting storefront studies, deliberately a composite concept rather than a verified block. Traditional 1990s Japanese RPG top-down three-quarter orthographic view, square tile ground plane, parallel building edges, no horizon, NOT diamond isometric, NOT 3D render. Crisp deliberate pixel clusters, warm airy daytime, cream concrete, muted teal glass, restrained saturated red and green accents. A small original white-robed wandering wizard with a tall triangular white hat and tiny charcoal face stands on the pavement, 2.5-head proportions, readable against the street, inspired by the quiet simplicity of Ida from Monument Valley but with an original short cape and silhouette. Character occupies about 5 percent of image height. Building upper floors selectively cropped to keep routes and shopfronts readable. Ground-level spatial readability, wide walkable pavement, authentic dense Hong Kong rhythm. No battle UI, no quests, no dialogue, no fantasy medieval elements, no cyberpunk, no bloom, no blur, no realistic rendering. Only minimal necessary signage, no decorative fake Chinese paragraphs. This is an art-direction painting in pixel-art language, not a production tileset.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: special scenic lookout illustration for a 2D pixel-art Hong Kong walking game. Wide 16:9. View from Tsim Sha Tsui waterfront looking south across Victoria Harbour, with Hong Kong Island skyline and a recognisable triangular cross-braced Bank of China Tower on the FAR shore across a broad stretch of turquoise water; mountain ridge behind the skyline. Foreground Tsim Sha Tsui promenade railings, paving, a bench and the small white triangular-hatted, white-robed wizard viewed from behind gazing across the water. A Star Ferry crosses at middle distance. Warm late afternoon shifting into soft blue evening; pixelated water ripples and lights. Traditional Japanese RPG pixel-art background painting, precise blocky pixel clusters, sophisticated restrained palette, atmospheric depth achieved with color bands, no blur, no glossy 3D. This is a deliberately composed optional lookout vista, NOT the top-down gameplay camera and NOT a map. Keep Bank of China Tower on Hong Kong Island, never on Kowloon; do not cram all Hong Kong landmarks together. Wizard has original 2.5-head tiny silhouette, charcoal face recess, short split white cape, triangular white hat. No UI, no title, no text, no watermark.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: pixel-art character art-direction sheet for an original non-combat Hong Kong walking RPG protagonist. On a warm light grey opaque studio background, show one original miniature wandering wizard consistently in four cardinal views (front, back, left, right) across the upper row; below show four walking pose studies, and a small palette swatch strip. White tall triangular hat, white short robe and short split cape, tiny charcoal face recessed under hat, small warm-grey boots, 2.5-head chibi proportions, no weapon, no staff, no backpack. Quiet architectural simplicity reminiscent of Ida in Monument Valley, but an original broader triangular hat folded at the back and shorter cape. Crisp pixel clusters and clean silhouette, ivory-white lights with blue-grey shadow pixels; dark outline only where needed. Every figure separated with generous space, equal size and aligned feet. Intended eventual game sprite canvas 32x48 pixels, enlarged by nearest-neighbour visual language for presentation. Important: this is a concept study and not a guaranteed frame-exact production sprite sheet. No labels, no typography, no 3D, no anti-aliased vector, no gradients, no blurry shadows, no paper texture.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: low-resolution gameplay art-direction mockup, original 2D pixel RPG set in Hong Kong. A compact single gameplay screen outside the Xiqu Centre near Canton Road and Austin Road West in West Kowloon. Recognisable curved silver theatre facade with a large central draped arch opening in the upper third, a paved public forecourt in the middle, a small tree bed, entrance steps and a nearby Hong Kong road edge. A white robed tiny wizard with a triangular white hat walks in the forecourt. STRICT classic SNES Japanese RPG visual grammar: top-down three-quarter orthographic, aligned horizontal and vertical square tile ground grid, no diamond isometric, no vanishing points, no horizon, no visible distant skyscraper panorama. Appearance of a native 320x180 game screen enlarged by exact nearest-neighbour into a 16:9 image: large clearly visible square pixel clusters, no subpixel detail, no vector lines, no fine texture. 16x16 tile design language, character approximately 16x24 logical pixels. Limited 32-color palette: cream pavement, silver-blue facade, jade trees, subdued red transit accents. Simplify the theatre's architectural curves into readable stepped pixel silhouettes. Keep upper storeys cropped, large walkable empty paving visible. Two tiny background pedestrian silhouettes maximum. No text, no UI, no combat, no quest marker, no 3D lighting, no glow, no gradients, no photorealism, no painterly textures. This must feel like a playable modest 1990s JRPG town screen, NOT a high resolution architectural concept painting. A conceptual facade and forecourt study, not a surveyed reconstruction.
